name: – Eric Sargiacomo – Draft Council decision
title: RECOMMENDATION on the draft Council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the European Union, of the Protocol on the implementation of the Fisheries Partnership Agreement between the European Community and the Republic of Guinea-Bissau (2024–2029)
part_text:
The European Parliament agrees that the European Union should sign a new five-year fishing deal with Guinea-Bissau, covering 2024 to 2029. The EU will pay 17 million euros a year: 12.5 million for the right of EU boats to fish in Guinea-Bissau's waters, and 4.5 million to help the country manage its fisheries and support local fishing communities. Boat owners also pay licence and catch fees. Parliament asks to be kept fully informed at every stage.

- EU boats from several member states may fish in Guinea-Bissau's waters under the new five-year deal.
- It affects EU fishing crews and shipowners, and people in Guinea-Bissau who depend on fishing.
- The deal applies provisionally since 18 September 2024; Parliament has now given its consent.
